Subject: Fit snapshot + pilot playbook — Redwood perf profiles and next steps

Hi Tom / Sally —

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and helpful context on the clinical summarization use case and expected doc sizes. Quick recap and a recommended, low-friction path to a 2-week pilot: 

Summary of our fit assessment (high level)
- Primary workload: multi-document summarization + entity tagging, median input ~1.2k tokens, 95th percentile ~4.5k tokens (after stitching).
- Quality requirement: high factuality on medical content; customer-led evals will include recall on annotated sections and hallucination checks on entity mentions.
- Latency sensitivity: interactive editing flows (target p95 generation < 1.5s for summary completions).

Recommended model shortlist (balanced quality / cost / latency) — Redwood-verified profiles attached:
1) redwood-llama3-70b-q8 (instruct) — best parity for clinical accuracy, recommended for gold-path QA; perf snapshot: 12 TPS at 512-context (single-stream), median latency 82ms/token, p95 end-to-end completion latency ~1.1s for 512 tokens.
2) redwood-7b-8bit-chat — cost-efficient fallback for high-throughput batches; perf snapshot: 48 TPS @ 512, median latency 24ms/token, p95 completion ~0.45s.
3) redwood-7b-longform (windowed) — recommended for 2–5k token inputs using streaming + prefix cache; TPS depends on prefix cache hit-rate (see appendix).

Key Redwood-verified metrics (attached PDF) — examples from our test harness using your sample prompt set:
- 512-token generation: redwood-llama3-70b-q8 — TPS 12, p50 78ms/token, p95 120ms/token; redwood-7b-8bit-chat — TPS 48, p50 22ms/token, p95 40ms/token.
- 2048-token end-to-end: redwood-llama3-70b-q8 — p95 completion latency ~3.9s (streaming for chunks), recommended to enable streaming with the UI.

Quality/regression notes
- The 70B variant shows measurably lower hallucination on entity prompts in our annotated suite; however, it is more sensitive to prompt drift — we recommend a guarded regression suite (we've included a starter set in the prompt bundle).
- For the 7B quant options, we see small degradation on niche medical terms; we suggest including targeted examples in the pilot eval to validate.

Pilot playbook (2 weeks) — suggested sequence
1) Week 0 (this week): exchange a small sample of redacted documents (5–10 cases) + pick the prompt set from the attached medix_promptset_v1.zip.
2) Week 1: run Redwood-hosted evals with our verifier harness (we'll share the bench run link). Focus: hallucination checks, entity recall, and throughput under expected concurrency.
3) Week 2: production-like pilot on a reserved Redwood Dedicated pool (we'll provision a small pool with canary routing). Finalize SLA targets and success gates by day 10.

Next actions I can own:
- Share the Redwood perf pack and prompt bundle (attached) — DONE.
- Provision a dedicated pilot pool (requested) and share credentials for your infra team to push brief smoke tests.
- Kick off the evaluation run using your sample set once you share redacted files.

Can you confirm: 1) you'll share 5–10 sample cases by end of week, and 2) your TPM prefers pilot start on Monday 2028-02-27 or earlier?

Attachments: redwood_perf_profiles_medix-20280221.pdf; medix_promptset_v1.zip; bench-traces-medix-20280221.json

Thanks,
Marissa

Tom / Sally — looping in a couple quick configuration suggestions from an infra/ops perspective to keep the pilot tight on both latency and cost:

- Prefix caching: enable prefix/KV cache on the 70B runs for conversational workflows — we typically observe ~30–45% token savings on multi-turns when the document context is reused. That keeps the p95 completion latency under the 1.5s SLO you mentioned.
- Batching policy: use continuous batching with a max batch wait of 10ms in the dedicated pool for the 7B fallback to maximize TPS without increasing p95 much.
- Quantization profile: for the pilot, try q8_0 on the 70B to retain factuality; if you need a cheaper run, we can swap to q4_0 on non-critical paths.
- Canary rollout: we'll set a 5% canary for the first 24h of the dedicated pilot and watch these KPIs: p95 latency, tokens-per-request, and hallucination rate on the regression set.

I've attached a short checklist in the bench run link with exact runtime flags and a recommended instance SKU. Marissa — I can spin up the dedicated pool once we have the sample files (I estimate ~4 hours to provision and warm caches).

—Karthik

Two small clarifications:
- If you plan to test long documents (3–5k tokens), enable streaming in the client and the 70B pipeline; that reduces the perceived latency for users even if total compute is higher.
- For the quality gates, we suggest the initial threshold: hallucination rate < 6% on the pilot regression set and entity recall > 90% for the top-10 clinical entities. We can iterate this once we see your samples.

I'll provision the dedicated pool after you drop the redacted files to the Drive link above or reply-all with a secure transfer method.
